label: Maya (career switcher)
tagline: Four years from marketing craft to a UX career switch: restlessness, research, and reps.

entries.title: Marketing coordinator, day one
entries.body: Started at the agency. Everyone says 'synergy' unironically. Keeping a private list of what actually works versus what gets applause in the room.

entries.title: Analytics certification done
entries.body: Finished the analytics cert on nights and weekends. Funnels, cohorts, attribution caveats. Numbers are arguments, and now I can make them.

entries.title: Marcus Chen — my manager
entries.body: Marcus Chen manages the growth team. Gives specific praise and specific criticism, both rare. If I ever manage anyone, I'm copying his one-on-one notes habit.

entries.title: Interviews beat dashboards
entries.body: Our dashboard said the landing page converted fine. Five customer calls said nobody understood the headline. The calls were right. Led with interviews every quarter since.

entries.title: First real budget
entries.body: Promotion bump finally budgeted properly: emergency fund to three months, retirement auto-transfer on. Future me says thanks in writing, here, so she can't deny it.

entries.title: The 25-minute weekly review
entries.body: Ten minutes clearing inboxes, ten reviewing the week against goals, five writing next week down. Timer visible, phone away. Three years unbroken.

entries.title: Running again
entries.body: Couch-to-5K, second attempt. Knees fine this time with slower ramps. Morning runs are when campaign ideas untangle themselves.

entries.title: Good at it, restless
entries.body: Another year-end review: exceeds expectations. And a quiet voice asking if applause is the point. Not a crisis. A draft of a question.

entries.title: UX keeps finding me
entries.body: Every research project I volunteer for is secretly a UX project: interviews, synthesis, flows. Read three job posts tonight. The pattern is not subtle anymore.

entries.title: Six-month craft experiment
entries.body: Decision: six months of deliberate UX learning before changing anything drastic. Input before output, reps before portfolio. Start September.

entries.title: Apartment lease, renewed
entries.body: Renewed the lease for one more year — the career experiment needs a stable base. Studio district can wait until the craft is real.

entries.title: Told Marcus first
entries.body: Told Marcus Chen about the UX experiment before telling anyone else. He asked good questions and offered introductions when I'm ready. Specificity is a gift to people helping you.

Six years in marketing and I am good at it, which is exactly the problem. I want a craft where the work itself is the reward, not the campaign metrics. UX feels right: research, structure, taste. Giving myself six months before I decide anything drastic.
entries.title: Why UX, why now

entries.body: This week: one UI teardown a day, twenty minutes, no more. Read the first three chapters of The Design of Everyday Things. No portfolio work yet — input before output.
entries.title: Week 1 plan

entries.body: UX is the whole journey and whether it works. UI is the surface and whether it sings. Product design is both plus strategy. Job posts mix them freely, so I will learn the full stack and let titles sort themselves out.
entries.title: UX vs UI vs product design

entries.body: Expires March 2028. Renewal needs: current passport, one photo, form DS-82, fee. Passport No: X7421980. Keep the number out of anything shared — this entry stays personal.
entries.title: Passport renewal checklist

entries.body: Years of customer interviews for campaigns transfer directly: same open questions, same hush after an interesting answer, same synthesis into themes. The method is identical; only the artifact changes from creative brief to user story.
entries.title: Marketing research maps to user research

entries.body: Priya Nair, product designer, six years. Met at the spring portfolio review night. Offered to review my first case study draft. Coffee every few weeks; she gives direct feedback and expects me to act on it.
entries.title: Priya Nair — mentor

entries.body: Looked at senior portfolios today and felt about four years behind. Then I noticed every one of them describes the same arc: messy middle, one constraint that forced the idea, a before and after. I can already do that shape. I just need the reps.
entries.title: First portfolio panic

entries.body: Pick one screen from an app you use daily. Twenty minutes, timer on. Write what each element is doing, then what you would change and why. Stop when the timer stops. The constraint matters more than the insight.
entries.title: The 20-minute UI teardown

entries.body: Twelve-month lease signed June. Rent due on the 1st, deposit was one month. Renewal window opens in April — decide by March whether to stay or move closer to the studio district.
entries.title: Lease agreement notes

entries.body: Affordances: what an object invites you to do. Signifiers: how it tells you. Mappings: whether controls match their effects. Most bad design is a signifier problem, not a user problem. Norman's door example finally clicked when I pictured our office doors.
entries.title: Notes: The Design of Everyday Things, ch. 1-3

entries.body: Ana Reyes, fellow career-switcher from teaching. We swap teardowns every Sunday over video call. Sharp eye for spacing rhythm; I help her with research framing.
entries.title: Ana Reyes — design buddy

entries.body: Seven teardowns in seven days. Quality varied wildly but the habit held, which was the actual goal. Next week: add the checklist so the teardowns stop being vibes-only.
entries.title: Teardown week one, done

entries.body: Right wrist aches after long Figma sessions. Reminder to self: track this, take breaks, and see someone if it persists past two weeks. Not sharing this — health stays personal.
entries.title: Wrist check

entries.body: Annual physical results: blood pressure fine, cholesterol slightly high at 212. Doctor suggested diet tweaks and a recheck in six months. Filed the lab printout with this note.
entries.title: Annual physical — lab summary

entries.body: Freeform teardowns kept circling the same observation: 'the hierarchy is unclear.' A checklist forces coverage — spacing, contrast, touch targets, empty states — and the interesting notes hide in the boxes I almost skip.
entries.title: Teardowns need a checklist

entries.body: My current pass, in order: 1) What is the one job of this screen? 2) Does the visual hierarchy agree? 3) Spacing rhythm — consistent 4/8 grid? 4) Contrast and touch targets. 5) Empty, loading, and error states. 6) One thing I would change, with a reason tied to the job.
entries.title: My teardown checklist, v1

entries.body: Coffee with Priya, product designer for six years. Her advice: one great case study beats four shallow ones, and hiring managers skim for decisions, not deliverables. She offered to review my first draft. I nearly said it wasn't ready — glad I said yes instead.
entries.title: Coffee with a real designer

entries.body: Marcus Chen, my former marketing manager. Knows my work better than anyone and offered introductions when I start applying. Keep him posted monthly; specificity is a gift to people helping you.
entries.title: Marcus Chen — former manager

entries.body: Auto-layout is flexbox with training wheels, and that is a compliment. Frames hug or fill; constraints handle the rest. The breakthrough: nest frames the way the layout actually works instead of fighting one giant frame. Redid my practice screen in half the layers.
entries.title: Figma auto-layout, finally clicked

entries.body: Tetanus booster due spring 2027. Flu shot done last week at the pharmacy. COVID booster current. Keeping this list updated so forms take seconds.
entries.title: Vaccination record

entries.body: Case study one: the checkout flow teardown, expanded. Sections: the problem I chose, the constraint (mobile, one thumb), three decisions with sketches, what I would test next. Draft by end of week four.
entries.title: Case study outline

entries.body: W-2 from the agency arrived. Still expecting the 1099 from the freelance brand sprint. Folder so far: W-2, three quarterly estimates, donation receipts. Start the return in February, not April.
entries.title: Tax folder 2026

entries.body: The portfolios that hold attention read as decision stories: here was the problem, here was the constraint, here is what I chose and what it cost. Deliverables are evidence, not the plot. My draft currently has the ratio backwards.
entries.title: Case studies are decision stories

entries.body: Audited three strong portfolios for structure: all open with the problem in one line, show at most two explorations, and end with measurable outcomes or honest unknowns. Ana spotted the pattern first — credit where due.
entries.title: Competitive audit: three portfolio sites

entries.body: Week four and the beginner high is gone. Teardowns feel repetitive, the case study is a mess, and everyone online seems faster. Writing it down to test it later: I suspect this is the dip, not the verdict.
entries.title: Imposter syndrome, week 4

entries.body: Dev Okafor, frontend developer I met at a Figma meetup. Answers my auto-layout questions in exchange for research help. Knows the handoff side cold — exactly the perspective my case studies lack.
entries.title: Dev Okafor — Figma wizard

entries.body: Thirty minutes, two people, timer visible. Each person gets ten minutes: two to present, eight for questions. Last ten minutes: each person states the one change they will make. No vague praise allowed — every compliment must name the decision it praises.
entries.title: Portfolio swap format that works

entries.body: Cleaning plus a small filling on the upper left. Dentist recommended a night guard for grinding — quoted, thinking it over. Next cleaning in six months.
entries.title: Dentist: cleaning + night guard

entries.body: Junior UX ranges in this city cluster around 70-90k, higher with research skills. My marketing salary is inside that band, so a switch does not require a pay cut if I position research as the bridge. Revisit with real offers, not job posts.
entries.title: Junior UX salary bands

entries.body: Priya's estimate from reviewing juniors: six minutes per portfolio on the first pass. Implication: the first screen of each case study must carry the problem, my role, and the outcome. Everything else is appendix.
entries.title: Hiring managers skim in 6 minutes

entries.body: Draft done: 1,400 words, six images, three decisions I can defend. Sending to Priya tonight. Whatever she says, the next draft gets the decision-story structure from my October 2 note.
entries.title: Case study draft done

entries.body: Reusable skeleton: problem in one line, my role, the constraint, two explorations max, the decision and its cost, outcome or honest unknown, what I would test next. Dev says engineers skim for the constraint first.
entries.title: Case study outline template

entries.body: Asked Marcus for an intro to the design lead at her company. Kept it specific: fifteen minutes, portfolio feedback, no ask for a job. Specificity is a gift to the person helping you.
entries.title: Asked my mentor for an intro

entries.body: Five applications out, two replies so far. Both replies came from referrals, zero from cold posts. Lesson holding: the network is the application. Tracking in the week 7 note.
entries.title: Application tracker — week 6

entries.body: Six weeks of teardowns plus the checklist habit. Can now read a screen's hierarchy, spacing rhythm, and state coverage cold. Next: motion and micro-interaction vocabulary.
entries.title: Interaction basics

entries.body: The insight was never the point; the reps were. Thirty teardowns built a reflex: I now see hierarchy and state coverage before I see style. Taste is a trained pattern-matcher, and pattern-matchers need data.
entries.title: What six weeks of teardowns taught me

entries.body: Next phase: applications plus a second case study from the portfolio swap. Keep the teardown habit at three per week — maintenance dose. Review this whole arc monthly.
entries.title: Next: applications
